content.title: About
content.content: Bloody Mary is a ready‑to‑mix blend for making the classic Bloody Mary cocktail, containing tomato juice, spices, flavorings, and sometimes a pinch of salt. It is designed for quick and convenient preparation at home.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Bloody Mary cocktail originated in the United States in the 1920s and quickly became popular as a "hair of the dog" drink.
Tomato juice gives the drink its rich flavor and bright red color, while spices like Worcestershire sauce, Tabasco, and black pepper provide characteristic heat.
Bloody Mary is often served with celery stalks, olives, pickles, or shrimp as garnish.
The drink is believed to help relieve hangovers thanks to the vitamins and antioxidants in tomatoes.
Various countries have their own twists, adding horseradish, soy sauce, or even bacon.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomato juice is a good source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6 and folate (B9), important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Electrolytes
items.content: Salt and tomato juice provide sodium and potassium, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory compounds
items.content: Spices such as black pepper and Worcestershire sauce contain compounds with anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Tomato juice and spices stimulate gastric secretions, aiding digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The added salt can be problematic for people with hypertension; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Spicy flavor
items.content: Tabasco and Worcestershire sauce make the drink very hot, which may irritate sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to components like soy sauce or anchovies found in Worcestershire sauce.

items.title: Acidity of tomato juice
items.content: The acidic nature can exacerbate heartburn in those with gastritis or reflux.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix 200 ml of the blend with 50 ml of vodka, add ice, and garnish with a celery stalk, olive, or lemon wedge. Optional additions include lime juice, horseradish, or bacon for variations.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the packet in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and use within 3–4 days. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
